Understanding Memory Allocation in Go

By Jane Doe | Published on August 10, 2026

When developing high-throughput services in Go, understanding how memory is allocated between the stack and heap is critical for performance tuning and minimizing garbage collection overhead.

The Go compiler performs escape analysis during compilation to determine whether a variable's lifetime exceeds the scope of its enclosing function. If a variable escapes, it is allocated on the heap; otherwise, it remains on the fast, automatically reclaimed stack.

You can inspect escape analysis decisions using the -gcflags="-m" compiler flag. Reducing heap allocations through struct pooling (using sync.Pool) and passing values by copy when appropriate can yield dramatic improvements in latency and CPU utilization.
